stream.scotty.core.windowFunction.builtin

Class Quantile<InputType,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>

  • java.lang.Object
    • stream.scotty.core.windowFunction.builtin.Quantile<InputType,ValueType>
  • Type Parameters:
    InputType - type of the input tuples
    ValueType - type of the values
    All Implemented Interfaces:
    Serializable, AggregateFunction<InputType,Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType>,ValueType>, CloneablePartialStateFunction<Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType>>, CommutativeAggregateFunction<InputType,Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType>,ValueType>, InvertibleAggregateFunction<InputType,Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType>,ValueType>

    public class Quantile<InputType,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>
extends Object
implements InvertibleAggregateFunction<InputType,Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType>,ValueType>, CommutativeAggregateFunction<InputType,Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType>,ValueType>, CloneablePartialStateFunction<Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType>>
    Exact quantile of the values in a window, e.g. the median for Quantile.create(0.5).

    The q-quantile of n values is the value at rank ceil(q * n) in ascending order, counting from 1 (nearest-rank method). The result is always one of the values in the window. For example, the 0.5-quantile of 1, 2, 3, 4 is 2, and of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 it is 3. q * n is computed with decimal arithmetic, so the 0.3-quantile of 10 values is the 3rd smallest value. q must be in (0, 1]: q = 1 is the maximum, use Min for the minimum.

    Works for all Comparable values, e.g. numbers or strings. Values that compare as equal are counted as the same value. The partial aggregate counts how often each distinct value occurs (Quantile.ValueCounts), so its size grows with the number of distinct values in a slice or window. Quantile is invertible and commutative. To avoid copying the counts for each tuple, combine and invert update the first partial aggregate in place. Scotty clones a slice's partial aggregate with clone(ValueCounts) before it combines other slices into it, so slices are not modified. The quantile of an empty partial aggregate is null.

    Use create(double) if the input tuples are the values, or Quantile(double, ValueExtractor) to use a value extracted from each input tuple.

      • lift

        public Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType> lift(InputType inputTuple)
        Description copied from interface: AggregateFunction
        Transforms a tuple to a partial aggregate. For example, consider an average computation. If a tuple ⟨p,v⟩ contains its position p and a value v, the lift function will transform it to ⟨sum←v, count←1⟩, which is the partial aggregate of that one tuple.

      • combine

        public Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType> combine(Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType> partialAggregate1,
                                               Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType> partialAggregate2)
        Description copied from interface: AggregateFunction
        Computes the combined aggregate from partial aggregates. Each incremental aggregation step results in one call of the combine function. It is expected that this method returns new partial aggregate. This method is used in two ways. 1. To add a single element to the partial aggregate. 2. To merge two big partial aggregates (or slices) , for example for emitting a final window. For the second step it is needed to emit a completely new partial aggregate. This can involve a deep copy of the partial aggregates. To prevent this a AggregationFunction can implement CloneablePartialStateFunction. In this case copy provides a cloned partial aggregate as the first argument.
        Specified by:
        combine in interface AggregateFunction<InputType,Quantile.ValueCounts<ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>
        Parameters:
        partialAggregate1 - the first original partial aggregate or a cloned object iff the AggregationFunction implements CloneablePartialStateFunction
        partialAggregate2 - the second ordinal partial aggregate.
        Returns:
        combined PartialAggregate
